text:
deploy-bot: heads-up — main pipeline turned red immediately after the autosquash merge (commit 9f3b2c1). failing step: integration-graphql (smoke-e2e). job: https://ci.example.com/jobs/37211 :exclamation:
alex: on it, grabbing logs now. any idea if this is flaky or deterministic? :eyes:
maya: saw similar earlier in canary but it passed on rerun. might be timing around subscription setup.
sam: linking failing snippet from the job log:
```
AssertionError: expected 200 but got 503
at tests/integration/graphql/subscription.test.ts:42:12
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues:93:5)
```
leah: re-run request queued: CI rerun #37211 -> #37212 (owner: none). can someone take the rerun to see if it repros?
alex: i'll rerun now. if it flakes i'll bisect between 9f3b2c1 and parent. leaving a note to skip long flaky paths.
deploy-bot: rerun started: job 37212. ETA ~5m.
maya: if fails again, try reproducing locally: `./scripts/ci/run-smoke --focus graphql-integration --repeat 10` — helps catch timing flake.
sam: quick check — does this touch KV cache changes from the last PR? commit 9f3b2c1 touched cache ttl in transport layer.
aleх: (typo correction) alex: yes, the commits touched kv cache ttl. tagging @oncall to be aware in case we need to revert.
oncall-bot: @oncall paged: infra-oncall (pager duty) — check pipeline red on main.
leah: rerun finished: job 37212 -> still red, same 503 error at subscription handshake.
maya: ok reproducible. alex: please bisect if you can, otherwise we should revert that PR to restore green.
alex: starting quick bisect: testing parent 9f3b2c0 locally with smoke harness. will report in ~15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: tagging notes — do not autosquash additional commits to main until we have a plan. :white_flag:
alex: bisect quick update — parent green locally, 9f3b2c1 reproduces the 503. looks like the change to kv ttl altered connection timing for subscriptions. proposing revert for now, open a follow-up to fix the race. anyone oppose?
maya: +1 revert. we can open a follow-on PR to harden subscription handshake.
leah: created revert PR #37250 and queued hot rollback. deploy-bot: rollback applied to main, pipeline back to queued.
oncall-bot: incident note: rollback performed to restore CI green.
sam: thanks everyone for quick turnaround :thumbsup:
alex: will follow up with an integration test that simulates kv latency and add to smoke suite.
maya: assign the follow-up to alex and maya.
leah: closing thread once main pipeline reports green.
deploy-bot: main pipeline is green again after rollback. thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
